A negative balance is what the company owes it. Sub-resellers collect and earn on their top-level reseller.

resellerLedger.depositInvalid: Type an amount greater than zero, with up to two decimals.
resellerLedger.adjustmentHelp: A correction to what the reseller owes: a positive amount raises it, a negative one lowers it. Explain why in the note.
resellerLedger.adjustmentInvalid: Type a non-zero amount with up to two decimals; a minus sign lowers the balance.

resellerStatements.title: Statements
resellerStatements.help: A statement closes a past period of a top-level reseller's cash: what it owed at the start, every movement of the period by type, and what it owes at the end (or what the company owes it). The figures always come from its movements. Before one is drawn up, the reseller's paid invoices are checked against its commissions.

resellerCommissions.title: Commissions
resellerCommissions.help: A reseller earns its commission rate on the subtotal (before taxes) of every paid invoice of a client it brought in, whoever collected the money. Sub-resellers' clients earn at their top-level reseller's rate, on its account. A commission is reversed when its invoice stops being paid, and earned again if it is paid again. The reseller keeps it from the cash it collects: see Movements.
